bxps_recalibration.finding: bXPS=220 was calibrated against the stepped xpCostTable model in Sprint 24. Sprint 25 switched to exponential 2.94*exp(stat/55) without re-calibrating. The exponential model's compounding makes 60-stat-point gains significantly more expensive than the flat table entries, so bXPS needed to increase proportionally. K was subsequently recalibrated from 55 to 47 via CV minimisation across 5 Grant ×40 observations (CV=3.2%). bXPS was then re-derived at 676 — the integral form of the XP budget equation with K=47 gives Grant Tackling 120 ×40 gain=65.7 (actual 59–73 ✓).

evidence.note: Grant data is actual before/after stats, not game-predicted range. Mid-range used as best estimate.

bxps_recalibration.rationale: Mean of 4 estimates: 495, 455, 414, 409 → mean 443. Initially set to 450. After K was recalibrated from 55 to 47 via CV minimisation across 5 Grant ×40 observations (CV=3.2%), bXPS was re-derived using the integral form of the XP budget equation: gain = C₀×K×[exp((stat+gain)/K) - exp(stat/K)] / ageMult. Solving the Grant Tackling 120 ×40 observation (budget = 40×bXPS/5 = 8×bXPS total, divided across 5 stats) gives bXPS=676: budget integral yields gain=65.7 (actual 59–73 ✓). All Dallas observations also validate at bXPS=676 with budget=4×676/3=901 XP/stat (MARKING 139 → 11.9 ✓ vs [11,16], POSITIONING 194 → 4.1 ✓ vs [4,6], AGGRESSION 189 → 4.5 ✓ vs [4,6]).

controlled_tests.note: Ratio 2.43 is sub-linear. Exponential cost model alone should give ~3.65 ratio for this stat range. Remaining 33% sub-linearity unexplained.
